_about: The seed library: genre-free reasoning patterns from existing reasoning language (Sudoku's technique ladder, constraint propagation, Hall's theorem, chains of implication, proof by cases, Polya and Engel's problem-solving strategies), for the library test's seeded arms (docs/research-walkthrough-loop.md). Deliberately genre-free: genre techniques people have named (walkthrough-known.json) are left out so the rediscovery check still means something. `primitives` are the solver's type-free rule kinds (signatures.ts PRIMITIVE) each pattern rests on, so an insight filed under an entry can be set beside the step the solver used.

entries.name: only place
entries.template: {unit} needs {thing}, and {cell} is the only place left in it that can hold it, so it goes there
entries.when: a unit must contain something and all but one of its places are ruled out

entries.name: only option
entries.template: every option for {cell} but {value} is ruled out, so {cell} is {value}
entries.when: a cell has one possibility left

entries.name: saturated
entries.template: {clue} needs {n}, and exactly {n} undecided places can still supply it, so all of them do
entries.when: a count can only be met by using every remaining candidate
entries.source: constraint propagation (a count at its upper bound of candidates)

entries.name: satisfied
entries.template: {clue} already has its {n}, so every other place it touches is out
entries.when: a count is already met
entries.concludes: the rest of its cells are out
entries.source: constraint propagation (a count at its lower bound)

entries.name: locked subset
entries.template: {k} cells in {unit} can only take the same {k} options between them, so those options are used up there and leave the rest of {unit}
entries.when: k places share exactly k options (or k options share exactly k places)
entries.concludes: those options are removed from the unit's other cells
entries.source: Sudoku naked and hidden pairs/triples; Hall's marriage theorem

entries.name: intersection
entries.template: within {unit A}, {thing} can only be where {unit A} overlaps {unit B}, so {unit B} gets it there and nowhere else
entries.when: a requirement of one unit is confined to its overlap with another
entries.concludes: the other unit's cells outside the overlap are out

entries.name: cover and rows
entries.template: {n} lines each need {thing} only within the same {n} cross-lines, so those cross-lines are filled by them and nothing else
entries.when: n units' candidates for something lie in n crossing units
entries.concludes: the crossing units' other candidates are out
entries.source: Sudoku X-Wing and fish; double counting

entries.name: forbidden pattern
entries.template: {cell} can't be {value}: that would make {pattern}, which the rules forbid
entries.when: one value completes a banned local pattern
entries.source: constraint propagation over a local rule

entries.name: must connect
entries.template: {group} has to join the rest, and its only way out is through {cell}, so {cell} carries it on
entries.when: a group that must stay connected has a single exit
entries.concludes: the exit is part of it

entries.name: cut off
entries.template: if {cell} were {value}, {group} would be sealed off from the rest, so it isn't
entries.when: a choice would disconnect something that must stay connected

entries.name: out of reach
entries.template: nothing that could cover {cell} can reach it within its size or distance, so {cell} is {value}
entries.when: a cell is farther from every possible owner than they can stretch
entries.concludes: the cell takes the value left for unowned cells

entries.name: no early loop
entries.template: joining {a} to {b} would close a loop before everything is in it, so they aren't joined there
entries.when: a link would close a cycle that leaves other required parts outside

entries.name: dead end
entries.template: {point} has only one way left to continue, so the line goes that way (or it can't be visited at all)
entries.when: a path point has all but one option closed
entries.concludes: the remaining option is forced, or the point is empty

entries.name: parity
entries.template: {region} must be crossed an even number of times (or hold an even count), and {k} is already used, so {conclusion}
entries.when: an invariant fixes the parity of a count
entries.concludes: the last option is forced by parity

entries.name: extremes first
entries.template: {value} is the most (or least) extreme value, and {constraint} only allows it at {places}
entries.when: the largest or smallest value has fewer possible places

entries.name: counting both ways
entries.template: counting {thing} by {units A} gives {x} and by {units B} gives {y}, so {conclusion}
entries.when: two ways of totalling the same quantity disagree unless something holds

entries.name: chain
entries.template: if {cell A} is {x} then {cell B} must be {y}, which forces {cell C} to {z} … so either way {conclusion}
entries.when: a chain of forced implications links two possibilities
entries.concludes: a cell seen from both ends of the chain
entries.source: Sudoku alternating inference chains (strong and weak links); implication graphs

entries.name: try and fail
entries.template: suppose {cell} were {value}: then {consequence}, which breaks {rule}, so it isn't
entries.when: assuming one value leads quickly to a contradiction
entries.source: proof by contradiction; Sudoku forcing chains

entries.name: both cases agree
entries.template: {cell} is either {a} or {b}, and in both cases {other} ends up {value}
entries.when: every case of a two-way choice forces the same thing elsewhere

entries.name: one solution
entries.template: if {cells} were {value}, they could be swapped without breaking anything, giving two solutions, so they aren't
entries.when: a choice would leave an interchangeable pattern
